newsitem.title: CHINA: China November interest rate subsidy 4.04 pct.
newsitem.headline: China November interest rate subsidy 4.04 pct.

text.p: China's central bank, the People's Bank of China, set the interest rate subsidy on deposits of three or more years at 4.04 percent, the Financial News said on Wednesday.
The subsidy showed a rise from 3.62 percent set for October and 3.61 percent in September. The rate had been falling since April.

China said in March it would stop paying interest rate subsidies on new deposits of three years and above from April 1 as inflation eased. Falling inflation would enable China to stop paying the subsidy by end-1996 or early next year, state media has said.
Such subsidies would continue to be paid on fixed deposits made before April 1.
On fixed deposits of three, five and eight years, banks currently pay interest rates of 12.24 percent, 14.94 percent and 17.64 percent.
The subsidy, designed to protect depositors against inflation, was reintroduced in March, 1994, when the rate was 1.19 percent. It hit a record of 13.24 percent in December 1995.
Retail price inflation was a year-on-year 6.6 percent in the first nine months of this year.
